summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of redo aortic valve replacement and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was readmitted for worsening shortness of breath and a large right pleural effusion. She also reported left-sided weakness and tongue deviation, with evaluation revealing mild dysarthria. Her INR was elevated on admission, requiring IV vitamin K before thoracentesis. A pigtail catheter was placed, draining 1400 cc of serosanguinous fluid. A small procedural pneumothorax resolved spontaneously. She was treated with renally dosed levofloxacin for suspected pneumonia and continued hemodialysis. Warfarin was resumed once INR stabilized. Speech therapy recommended outpatient follow-up for dysarthria. She improved clinically, with resolution of respiratory symptoms and stable cardiac status, and was discharged home with services on hospital day 6 when her INR was therapeutic.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Heart valve replaced by other means
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
